all_of: a hand-rolled template engine substitutes values with String.replace and a string pattern
a headless browser can be pointed at a page of the attacker's choosing
any_of: a per-response nonce is substituted into the same template before the user-controlled field
one view reflects a parameter without the escaping the other views apply
a privileged action is gated on a custom request header

chain.action: read the template helper before the views: if substitution is done with String.replace(pattern, value) then the $ replacement patterns are live - $-backtick expands to the text before the match and $-apostrophe to the text after
chain.why: a replace-based renderer turns any user field into a primitive for copying other parts of the same line into the output

chain.action: check the substitution ORDER against the object's key order; anything substituted earlier on the same line is now reachable through $-backtick
chain.why: the per-response nonce was substituted first, so the user field could copy the live nonce - no markup required, which is why the escaping on that field was irrelevant

chain.action: land the payload inside the EXISTING nonced script element rather than trying to create one: $-backtick reproduces the prefix (ending in the opening quote of a string literal), so append a terminator, the code, and a line comment
chain.why: reusing a legitimate nonce defeats a nonce-based script-src completely, and the escape filter only removes markup characters

chain.action: respect the escape filter when writing the JS: no angle brackets, ampersand, or either quote - so use backticks, function(){} instead of arrow functions, and carry any markup base64-encoded through atob()
chain.why: an arrow function contains a closing angle bracket and would be neutered by the escaper

chain.action: from inside the bot issue a SAME-ORIGIN fetch to the privileged endpoint with the custom header, and include a urlencoded body plus content-type
chain.why: a custom header cannot be set by a form, so the gate is really demanding script execution; and on Express 5 req.body is undefined unless a parser matched, so a bodyless POST makes the handler throw

chain.action: the privileged branch sends the bot to the reflecting view with the secret in the query string: inject a title-closing tag, a referrer meta set to unsafe-url, and a meta refresh, then read the full URL out of the Referer on your listener
chain.why: this CSP restricts every subresource to self but nothing restricts navigation, so the victim page's own URL is the exfil channel

first_confirming_probe.request: request the templated page with the user field set to a single $-backtick and read the raw response
first_confirming_probe.expected: the line is duplicated: the text preceding the placeholder (including anything already substituted, such as a nonce) appears inside the value
first_confirming_probe.falsifier: the two characters come back literally, meaning the renderer does not use String.replace with a string pattern

blast_radius: negligible. The application has no datastore, no session and no upload - the only side effect is launching a short-lived headless browser per request, and nothing persists between runs. There is nothing to clean up afterwards.

verification.evidence: the listener received the navigation with the full victim URL, including the flag parameter, in the Referer header

reuse_when: a template is rendered with String.replace and user data is the replacement
a nonce-based CSP is paired with a template that already emits a nonced script element
a strict CSP blocks subresources but the victim page holds the secret in its own URL
a privileged branch is gated on a custom header, implying script execution is required
known_traps: a free tunnel that shows an abuse interstitial keys on USER-AGENT, so it silently swallows every request a headless browser makes - navigation, script src and images alike. A curl smoke test passes and misleads you into reading 'no callback' as 'exploit failed'. Always re-test the listener with a browser User-Agent before trusting a negative result.
the default referrer policy is strict-origin-when-cross-origin, which drops path and query - without a referrer meta set to unsafe-url the callback arrives with only the origin and no secret

Express 5 leaves req.body undefined when no body parser matched, so a fetch without a content-type makes a destructuring handler throw 500 and the chain dies silently; have the payload report the response status back to the listener to find this

script.src is a TrustedScriptURL sink, so under require-trusted-types-for it throws unless a policy is created; navigation is not a Trusted Types sink, which makes the meta-refresh route the robust one
an arrow function cannot survive an escaper that strips angle brackets - use function(){} instead
the reflecting placeholder may sit inside a title element, whose contents parse as text: open with a title end tag or the injected markup is inert
